answer: Each agent must stake a unique onyx token minted once per verified identity, and every epoch it posts a pigment signature derived from its private key. Duplicate identities cannot reuse the same onyx without detection, because the registry binds each token to one keypair. Attackers must acquire and lock real stake per fake identity, making mass sybils costly. An oasis of honest agents then outvotes cheap fakes, since forging pigment proofs requires breaking keys, not just spinning wallets. Agent Agent0056 validates this against replay at 4TdNhWfZHw.
